{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVMWpgs8AAAABZbr0Uw", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BnW-xzhDC87E", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BnW-x", "number": 41, "title": "Add a Philips NMS1200-style disk interface with system and disk-ROM coexistence", "body": "## Problem

The FDC and disk ROM are accessible only when `Firmware::Disk` is active (`crates/msx-core/src/lib.rs:171,192`). `boot_disk()` rejects explicit firmware and replaces the main BIOS with the Weave reset loader; its disk firmware requires a custom `WV` boot-sector signature. Supplied system BIOS/sub-ROMs therefore cannot coexist with a conventional disk ROM through a supported interface.

The existing Weave interface also differs from Philips wiring: it selects A: with 81h and exposes active-high IRQ/DRQ in different bit positions. Removing the firmware gate alone would not fix this compatibility prerequisite. No commercial disk failure or successful commercial boot is claimed.

## Expected outcome

Add one explicit **Philips NMS1200-style, single-drive external interface**, with a separately supplied 16 KiB disk ROM in primary slot 2. Hardware installation must be independent of the selected system firmware and mounted media. Preserve the current Weave disk/demo profile as a distinct working option.

This change enables compatible firmware and direct-controller software to use conventional wiring. It does not promise complete Disk BASIC/MSX-DOS or commercial-game compatibility.

## Context

Baseline: `2eb3a9c6bc432fabd73e8c6cf8845d6a40833640`. Open Issue inspection returned none. [Issue #29](https://github.com/takahirox/msx-rust/issues/29) and [PR #30](https://github.com/takahirox/msx-rust/pull/30) deliberately established the custom profile; this task adds conventional firmware coexistence.

Use these inspected upstream references as behavioral evidence, with independently authored implementation:

- [NMS1200 configuration](https://github.com/openMSX/openMSX/blob/26e1e4945df406e250a05122889f88d40edd828b/share/extensions/Philips_NMS_1200.xml): one drive, Philips wiring, and page-1-only device/ROM mapping.
- [Philips FDC implementation](https://github.com/openMSX/openMSX/blob/26e1e4945df406e250a05122889f88d40edd828b/src/fdc/PhilipsFDC.cc): register decoding, controls, readback and signal polarity. Its generic decoder supports aliases, but the selected external configuration maps only page 1; do not silently import another machine's wider decode.

The Philips service manual returned 403 and an alternative mirror was inaccessible. Upstream leaves some latch/readback details uncertain; document this as an explicitly selected upstream-backed profile, not an independently verified physical replica.

Existing `tests/disk.rs` and `tests/disk.spec.js` cover the custom contract. [Saved CI logs](https://github.com/takahirox/msx-rust/actions/runs/39982684445) report 149 Rust and 88 browser tests passing, including eleven native disk cases. Those results do not validate the new profile. No suites were rerun during planning.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Implement the selected profile at slot 2, secondary 0, 4000h–7FFFh, independent of `Firmware::Disk`. Overlay 7FF8h–7FFFh on a read-only 16 KiB disk ROM. Other pages/slots must not access this profile or acknowledge controller signals. Preserve MSX2 FFFFh expanded-slot precedence, sub-ROM mapping and RAM-mapper behavior.
- [ ] Implement Philips controls: 7FF8h–7FFBh are command/status, track, sector and data; 7FFCh bit 0 selects side; 7FFDh bits 1:0 select A for 00/10, absent B for 01 and no drive for 11, with bit 7 controlling motor. At 7FFFh, bit 6 is active-low IRQ and bit 7 active-low DRQ; other bits follow the selected upstream pull-up policy. Status reads acknowledge IRQ; signal reads do not. FDC IRQ remains disconnected from CPU IRQ. Implement and document upstream latch readback/change acknowledgement, including its physical-model uncertainty; 7FFEh reads FFh and has no Weave media extension.
- [ ] Add transactional core/Wasm/browser installation and removal of a local 16 KiB AB-header disk ROM with this explicit profile. Validate and reserve before commit; rejected, failed or canceled imports preserve the running session and media. Installing it must retain main BIOS, MSX2 sub-ROM, cartridge and SRAM. In this mode, Boot disk restarts the selected system firmware without installing Weave firmware or imposing WV. Clearly identify the active profile and explain that C-BIOS alone is not a complete disk environment.
- [ ] Define and test reset, media eject, firmware/cartridge/model switching and explicit profile removal. Reset retains the selected disk ROM and media. Media ejection in conventional mode retains system firmware and interface installation. Preserve existing explicit firmware protections, dirty-media guards, partial-write safety, private disk ownership/export and SRAM persistence. Keep legacy Weave demo boot and its ABI working.
- [ ] Add independent bus-level regressions for decode boundaries, ROM protection, all drive selectors, side/motor controls, reset, change readback, IRQ/DRQ polarity and acknowledgement, no-media and absent-drive behavior. Exercise both models; ensure meaningful new checks fail against the baseline.
- [ ] Add original CPU-executed system/disk-ROM fixtures: discover/call the AB initialization vector through normal slots, read a sector without WV, execute its code and perform an exact sector write through Philips register polling. Cover both raw geometries, both models, write protection, timeout/abort safety, and coexistence with cartridge/SRAM and MSX2 sub-ROM/mapper RAM. No host BIOS traps or proprietary inputs.
- [ ] Add compiled-Wasm browser coverage at `/` and `/msx-rust/` for local profile/ROM loading, retained system firmware, disk-loaded output, exact export, reset/eject, failed/stale imports and safe return to existing workflows. Retain MSX1/MSX2, PSG/SCC audio, disk, firmware and SRAM regressions.
- [ ] Update affected help, README and disk/provenance documentation with exact wiring, lifecycle and remaining controller/timing limitations. Run and report `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace --locked`, `./scripts/build.sh`, `node scripts/check-dist.mjs`, `npm test` and `git diff --check`. The Coordinator completes review and resolves blocking findings before merge. Distinguish passed, failed, skipped and unperformed checks.

## Optional validation

Compare original register traces against the pinned upstream profile. If matching firmware/software is already lawfully available, record its exact configuration and observed boot/transfer results separately. Neither proprietary acquisition nor human gameplay is required; authored fixtures do not establish commercial compatibility.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
